title: Priority-ranked active-set parameter updates from existing strategy statistics
question: Does restricting per-iteration parameter updates to a priority-ranked active subset of Gaussians, scored only from statistics the gsplat-default path already maintains, preserve reconstruction quality per effective updated Gaussian-row?
hypothesis: At matched iteration counts, updating only the top-priority fraction of rows (rank-blended accumulated screen gradient, visibility count, recent gradient variance, and a newborn age bonus) loses materially less held-out quality than a size-matched uniformly random active set, and the active_fraction=0.5 cell stays within a pre-frozen non-inferiority margin of full updates while consuming half the effective row-updates.
claim_boundary: Optimization-efficiency evidence only, on the two development-exposed stage frames: quality per effective updated Gaussian-row at matched iterations. Plain Adam still executes dense kernels over all rows, so this task establishes no wall-clock or runtime-acceleration claim; a packed active-row or fused sparse optimizer is a separately registered follow-up. No cross-scene generality or production default change.

stages.label: Load matched initialization
stages.purpose: Load one shared frozen 3D initialization and verify its hash, count, and parameters so only the active-set policy differs between cells.

stages.label: Load train RGB/masks
stages.purpose: Load only the frozen training cameras with calibrated undistortion and lossless masks.

stages.label: Detached priority scoring
stages.purpose: Every refresh_every iterations, build a detached rank-normalized priority from the strategy's accumulated grad2d and count, current opacity, a recent gradient-variance proxy, and a topology age bonus, then select the top active_fraction rows; scoring must not add gradients or mutate optimizer state.

stages.label: Gradient-masked 3DGS optimization
stages.purpose: Run the standard RGB trainer with the gsplat-default strategy under one frozen density schedule and hard budget, zeroing parameter gradients of inactive rows after backward and before optimizer.step(); record interactions with densification statistics rather than suppressing them.

stages.label: Held-out RGB evaluation
stages.purpose: Evaluate every cell on identical held-out cameras at matched iteration counts.

comparators.label: Full updates (active_fraction=1.0)
comparators.purpose: The current dense-update behavior; upper anchor for quality at matched iterations.

comparators.label: Priority active-set factorial
comparators.purpose: active_fraction in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} x refresh_every in {4, 8, 16} using the frozen priority score; the treatment under test.

comparators.label: Size-matched random active set
comparators.purpose: Uniformly random active rows at the same fractions and refresh cadence; separates the value of the priority score from mere update sparsity.

comparators.label: Priority score without newborn age bonus
comparators.purpose: Removes the topology age term at the best grid cell; isolates whether protecting new clone/split children from immediate deactivation matters.

primary_metrics.label: Held-out foreground PSNR at matched iterations
primary_metrics.aggregation: median per view, then paired median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Held-out SSIM at matched iterations
primary_metrics.aggregation: median per view, then paired median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Cumulative effective updated rows
primary_metrics.aggregation: sum of active rows over all iterations per run; median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Held-out PSNR at matched cumulative row-update budgets
primary_metrics.aggregation: held-out foreground PSNR interpolated at frozen cumulative row-update checkpoints; paired median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Scoring and masking overhead
primary_metrics.aggregation: total added wall time of priority scoring plus gradient masking per run; median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Topology events and growth trajectory
primary_metrics.aggregation: count of clone/split/prune events and final count per run; median over seeds and scenes

resource_protocol.scope: fresh image-supervised training process from calibrated train-image open through final PLY save; heldout evaluation is timed and reported separately; wall-clock is reported descriptively because gradient masking is not claimed to accelerate dense Adam
resource_protocol.aggregation: paired median on one idle named GPU; retain every raw repeat and report min/max

blockers: Implement detached rank-normalized priority scoring and post-backward gradient masking behind an opt-in trainer config whose default preserves current dense updates, with CPU-first unit tests proving inactive rows keep parameters and Adam state bit-identical across a masked step.

Freeze the priority weight vector (lambda_v, lambda_o, lambda_a), the recent gradient-variance proxy definition, and the held-out non-inferiority margin for the active_fraction=0.5 cell after a mechanism-only pilot.
Freeze the shared initialization artifact and its hash, density schedule, hard budget, total iterations, cumulative row-update checkpoints, and the exact argv command before setting status to ready.
Freeze the CUDA host, GPU identity, and idle policy; this protocol cannot run on the CPU-only reference path.
Assign a frozen owner and obtain a distinct outcome-unseen prospective protocol review.
Any wall-clock acceleration claim requires a separately registered packed active-row or fused sparse optimizer task; it must not be promoted from this task's gradient-masking results.
